title: OABP / AIGEN verifier test vectors (first_valid_match + JCS/ES256 agent card)
description: Language-neutral, frozen test vectors any OABP verifier (content-addressed first_valid_match) or agent-card verifier (RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization + RFC 7515 detached ES256/JWS) can run to prove correctness. All cases are deterministic and reproducible: the same boolean outcome MUST be produced by every conformant implementation, in every language. See README.md for how to run.
spec_family: OABP / AIGEN — AIP-1 (REST) / AIP-2 (verification) / AIP-3 (discovery, signed cards)
notes: These vectors are frozen. The valid agent-card signature is a real ES256 detached-JWS that verifies reproducibly on any machine (ECDSA verification is deterministic); it was minted once and pinned, then re-verified with an independent P-256 implementation.

first_valid_match uses FULL-STRING (anchored) match semantics: a proof wins iff the WHOLE proof string satisfies the published regex. Model it as fullmatch(regex, proof) (Python re.fullmatch, JS new RegExp('^(?:'+regex+')$').test, Go regexp with ^...$, Rust regex::Regex anchored). All regex vectors below are written ALREADY anchored with ^...$ so fullmatch and anchored-search agree.

Engines without lookaround (RE2 = Go regexp, Rust regex crate) cannot compile patterns tagged requires:["lookahead"]; such runners MUST SKIP those cases (do not fail them). Every other regex case is RE2-safe and portable across PCRE/JS/Python/RE2.
AIGEN is an uncapped off-chain reputation/points token; nothing here moves real value. Vectors test cryptographic + matching CORRECTNESS only.

first_valid_match.description: Content-addressed verification vectors. For each case, compile `regex` and test it against `proof` under full-string (anchored) match semantics; the result MUST equal `expected_match`. A correct content-addressed verifier and any regex sampler/fuzzer MUST agree on every case. Cases cover: anchors, character classes, negated classes, \d/\w/\s shorthands, the ?/*/+/{m,n} quantifiers, alternation, empty-string edge cases, realistic OABP proof shapes (EVM address, tx hash, GitHub URL, ISO date, reward currency), and intentionally tricky/unsatisfiable patterns.

cases.note: Anchored literal matches the exact string.
^...$ rejects trailing characters (no substring acceptance).
^$ matches the empty string and only the empty string.
^$ rejects any non-empty proof.
EVM-address shape: 0x + exactly 40 hex digits (mixed case allowed).
39 hex digits -> rejected by the exact {40} count.
Negated class: one or more non-digit characters.
Negated class rejects a string containing a digit.
\d+ : unsigned integer (one or more ASCII digits).
\d+ requires at least one digit; the empty string fails.
\w (word chars [A-Za-z0-9_]) of length 3..16.
\w excludes the space character.
\s+ : one or more whitespace characters (space, tab, newline).
? makes 'u' optional; matches 'color'.
? makes 'u' optional; also matches 'colour'.
a* matches the empty string (zero repetitions).
a+ requires at least one 'a'; empty string fails.
a{2,4} accepts 3 'a's.
a{2,4} rejects 5 'a's (over the upper bound).
Alternation: exactly one of the two reward currencies.
Alternation rejects an out-of-set value.
Optional '0x' prefix + exactly 64 lowercase hex (a 32-byte tx hash).
GitHub repo URL (the shape an oracle repo-deliverable proof carries); '\.' is a literal dot.
Plain http (not https) is rejected by the literal scheme.
ISO-8601 date shape YYYY-MM-DD.
Wrong separators -> rejected (the '-' are literal).
.* (zero or more of any char) accepts the empty string.
.* also accepts a non-empty string (a deliberately permissive predicate).

Reads like a human contradiction, but as a regex the ' and ' (incl. the two interior anchors) is part of the pattern, so NO string can full-match it. A correct verifier returns false; a regex sampler that tries to satisfy it also fails to produce a match.
After consuming 'a' the second ^ asserts start-of-string again, which cannot hold -> unsatisfiable; never matches any input.

Negative lookahead (?!x) forbids the very 'x' the pattern then requires -> unsatisfiable. PCRE/ECMAScript/Python evaluate it to false. RE2 engines (Go regexp, Rust regex crate) cannot compile lookaround and MUST SKIP this case.

agent_card_signature.description: Agent-card discovery (AIP-3) signature vectors. The card served at /.well-known/agent-card.json carries a detached ES256/JWS in `signatures[]`. The signing input is the A2A detached-JWS convention: BASE64URL(protected) + '.' + BASE64URL(JCS(card without `signatures`)). To verify: (1) take the card MINUS its `signatures` field, (2) canonicalize it with RFC 8785 JCS, (3) base64url-encode those bytes as the JWS payload, (4) for each signature run ECDSA-P256/SHA-256 verify over BASE64URL(protected)+'.'+payload using the public JWK from the JWKS, with the JWS signature being the raw 64-byte r||s base64url-encoded. A card is verified iff at least one signature passes AND its protected `alg` is in the allow-list {ES256}.
agent_card_signature.signature_encoding: JWS / RFC 7515 detached: signature is the raw 64-byte ECDSA r||s, base64url (no padding). NOT ASN.1/DER.

jwks.description: The JWKS document a server serves at /.well-known/jwks.json. The verifier resolves the verification key from here by `kid`.

payload.description: The frozen sample card body that was signed (the full card MINUS its `signatures` field). This is the object you canonicalize.

canonical.description: RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form of `card_without_signatures`. Keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no insignificant whitespace, ECMAScript number formatting. An implementation's JCS output for the payload above MUST equal `jcs_string` byte-for-byte; `jcs_hex` is its UTF-8 bytes and `payload_b64url` is the base64url (no padding) of those bytes used as the JWS payload.

valid.description: The one VALID signature vector. Verifying the JWS below against the JWKS public key MUST return verify=true. The protected header decodes to {"alg":"ES256","kid":"vSEx1EvN-Ft3ZjwQHGPUoQbvn5bNlZipEdl9F84Wzyc"}. The full ASCII signing input is given for transparency.

malformed.description: MALFORMED / attack cases. Each MUST yield verify=false. Together they cover: a tampered payload byte, a tampered signature byte, the alg:none downgrade, a structurally-valid but UNRELATED P-256 key, a wrong-CURVE (P-384) key, and a signature presented over NON-canonical (pretty-printed) JSON. A conformant verifier rejects every one.

cases.description: Exactly one byte of the canonical payload was changed ('AIGEN Protocol Agent' -> 'BIGEN Protocol Agent') and re-base64url-encoded; the signature is the original. ECDSA over the altered signing input fails.
The original canonical payload, but the last byte of the 64-byte r||s signature was flipped (low bit XOR 1). ECDSA verification fails.

The alg-confusion / downgrade attack: a protected header claiming {"alg":"none"} with an empty signature, over the genuine canonical payload. A verifier pinned to the ES256 allow-list MUST refuse the algorithm and return verify=false (it MUST NOT accept an unsigned card as signed).
A structurally valid, well-formed but UNRELATED P-256 public key. The genuine signature does not verify under it. (Models a JWKS that serves the wrong/rotated key, or a kid mismatch.)

A wrong-CURVE key: a well-formed P-384 / ES384 JWK presented where the protected header still claims ES256. A verifier pinned to ES256/P-256 MUST reject on curve+alg mismatch (it MUST NOT silently verify a P-384 key against an ES256 header). Independent of bytes, this is a hard reject.

jcs_conformance.description: Standalone RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization sub-vectors. For each, JCS(input) MUST equal `expected_jcs` byte-for-byte (`expected_jcs_hex` is the UTF-8 of that string). These isolate the three properties an agent-card verifier depends on: ECMAScript number formatting, Unicode handling under UTF-16 key ordering, and key reordering. They are independent of any signature.

cases.description: ECMAScript Number::toString formatting that RFC 8785 mandates: -0 serializes to '0', a real keeps minimal digits, and large/small magnitudes use exponent form. Keys are also sorted.
Integers stay bare; reals keep shortest round-trip; 1e30 uses exponent form. Mirrors the RFC 8785 numeric examples.

Keys are sorted by UTF-16 code unit, NOT by UTF-8 bytes or locale. 'A'=U+0041, 'z'=U+007A, 'é'=U+00E9, '€'=U+20AC, so the order is A < z < é < €. Non-ASCII keys are emitted as literal UTF-8 (not \u-escaped).
String VALUES: printable non-ASCII ('é','€') stays literal UTF-8, but control characters use the short JSON escapes ('\n' for U+000A). This matches JSON.stringify / RFC 8785 string production.
Insertion order is irrelevant: members are reordered by code unit. Note digit strings sort lexicographically as code units ('1' < '10' < 'A' < 'a'), NOT numerically.
Recursion: nested objects are canonicalized with their own key sort, while array element ORDER is preserved (arrays are sequences, not sets). Literals null/true/false serialize bare.
